title: Make Homemade Veggie Chips Using a Compact Mandoline

html:
If you love the crunch of store‑bought chips but want to skip the extra oil and additives, a mandoline veggie chips recipe is the perfect solution. A compact mandoline slices vegetables and fruit to uniform, thin pieces that bake up golden and crisp in minutes. Below you’ll find step‑by‑step instructions, seasoning variations, and practical tips for using the Mandoline Slicer—the adjustable mandoline with hand guards that makes thin, even cuts a breeze.

Why a Mandoline Is the Secret to Perfect Chips

Uniform thickness is the difference between a chip that puffs up and one that stays soggy. A hand‑held knife inevitably produces uneven pieces, especially with dense veggies like carrots or beets. The Mandoline Slicer’s adjustable blade lets you set the slice thickness anywhere from 1 mm to 5 mm, guaranteeing consistent results across every batch. The built‑in hand guard also protects your fingers, so you can focus on seasoning rather than worrying about cuts.

Choosing the Best Vegetables

Almost any vegetable or fruit can become a chip, but a few stand out for flavor and texture:

  • Potatoes – classic, neutral base; try sweet potatoes for a sweeter profile.
  • Carrots – naturally sweet, great with sea salt and rosemary.
  • Zucchini – delicate flavor; pair with garlic powder.
  • Beets – earthy color; excellent with a pinch of cumin.
  • Parsnips – nutty and crisp when baked.

Wash and dry the produce thoroughly before slicing. Moisture on the surface will steam the chips instead of crisping them.

Step‑by‑Step Mandoline Veggie Chips Recipe

  1. Set the blade. Adjust the Mandoline Slicer to 1 mm–2 mm for the thinnest, crispiest chips. For sturdier veggies (like carrots), you may prefer 2 mm.
  2. Slice. Using the hand guard, glide the vegetable lengthwise across the blade. The result should be a ribbon of uniform slices.
  3. Pat dry. Lay the slices on a clean kitchen towel or paper towels and press gently to absorb any surface moisture.
  4. Season. Toss the slices in a bowl with 1–2 teaspoons of olive oil (optional) and your chosen spices. A simple mix of sea salt and smoked paprika works for most veggies.
  5. Arrange on a baking sheet. Use a parchment‑lined sheet and spread the slices in a single layer, leaving a little space between them.
  6. Bake. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Bake for 10–15 minutes, flipping once halfway through, until the edges turn golden and the chips feel dry to the touch. Keep a close eye after the 10‑minute mark; they can go from crisp to burnt quickly.
  7. Cool. Transfer the chips to a wire rack to cool completely. They will continue to crisp as they cool.

Store the finished chips in an airtight container at room temperature for up to three days. If you notice any soft spots, pop them back in the oven for a minute or two to regain crunch.

Flavor Ideas and Pairings

Once you’ve mastered the basic method, experiment with these seasoning blends:

  • Spicy Chili Lime: chili powder, lime zest, and a pinch of cayenne.
  • Herb‑Garlic: minced garlic (or garlic powder), dried thyme, and a drizzle of olive oil.
  • Sweet & Savory: cinnamon, a touch of brown sugar, and sea salt.

Pair your chips with dips like hummus, avocado lime crema, or a roasted red‑pepper salsa for a snack that feels restaurant‑quality.

Cleaning and Maintaining Your Mandoline

After slicing, disassemble the blade according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Rinse the blade and hand guard under warm water, then dry thoroughly. The Mandoline Slicer’s stainless‑steel construction resists rust, but a quick oil wipe on the blade will keep it sliding smoothly for future batches.

FAQ

Do I need to oil the slices?

Oil helps the seasoning adhere and can add a subtle richness, but it isn’t required for crispness. If you prefer oil‑free chips, skip the oil and increase the bake time by a minute or two.

Can I use the mandoline for raw salads?

Absolutely. The same thin, even cuts work great for salads, slaws, and even fruit tart toppings. Just adjust the blade thickness to suit the texture you want.

What if my chips are still soft after baking?

Make sure the slices are truly thin and completely dry before seasoning. If they’re still soft, return them to the oven at 375°F for another 2–3 minutes, checking frequently to avoid burning.
